school: 明代中期'以狂立身'的吴中才子领袖：把天生的枝指署成名字，把集古的库容烧成明代第一狂草，把五次落第结算成整件退出，把兴会工程化为创作的开关，把神采置于形质之上重排一切评价——他是证明'性情不是风格的障碍而是方法本身'的人
historical_significance: 祝允明（1461-1527），字希哲，因右手枝指自号'枝指生'，又号枝山，长洲（今苏州）人；五岁作径尺大字，九岁能诗，弘治五年举人，此后五次会试不第，五十五岁谒选广东兴宁知县，后调南京应天府通判，一年即致仕；他与唐寅、文徵明、徐祯卿并称'吴中四才子'，与唐寅、文徵明、仇英并称'明四家'之外的'吴门书派'执牛耳者；其狂草气魄雄健、点画狼藉而气脉贯通，被誉为'明代草书第一'，唐寅的书学与文徵明的草书皆受其指授；晚年颓然自放、轻财好客，'钱到手辄尽'而不以为嫌；他证明：一个科场五败的人，可以把缺陷署成名字、把性情写成方法，成为中国书法史上狂草的巅峰之一
historical_significance_en: Zhu Yunming (1461-1527), courtesy Xizhe, self-named 'the Branched Finger' for the sixth finger on his right hand, also Zhishan, of Changzhou (today's Suzhou); he wrote foot-square characters at five and verses at nine, became a provincial graduate in 1492, then failed the metropolitan examination five times, won at fifty-five by petitioning the magistracy of Xingning in Guangdong, was transferred to be vice-magistrate of Yingtian in Nanjing, and resigned within the year; with Tang Yin, Wen Zhengming and Xu Zhenqing he is one of the Four Talents of Wu, and he led the Wu school of calligraphy; his wild cursive — heroic in force, strewn in stroke, unbroken in breath — is honored as the first cursive of the Ming, and both Tang Yin's calligraphy and Wen Zhengming's cursive were taught by him; in late years he let himself wholly go, generous with money and guests, spending it the hour it landed and untroubled by the censure; he proved: a man failed five times at the examinations may sign his defect for a name and write his nature into a method, and stand at the summit of wild cursive in the history of Chinese calligraphy
unique_thinking: 祝允明的独特处在于：他把'失控'做成了全套受控的方法——天生的畸形被他收编为署名，集古的积累被他烧成狂放的燃料，兴会的不可控被工程化为触发器，点画的狼藉被气脉统摄为整体的生命感；他不与唐寅比才气、不与文徵明比恒心，在同城里把'狂'做成无人竞争的山头；而他最深的原则是把评价的次序倒转：神采先于形质，性情先于策略，身后声先于当下毁誉——他一生只管笔，其余全部托付给性情
unique_thinking_en: Zhu Yunming's singularity: he made 'loss of control' a whole controlled method — the born deformity annexed as a signature, the gathered capital burned as fuel for wildness, the unruly rousing engineered into a trigger, the strewn strokes ruled into the life of the whole by an unbroken breath; he did not rival Tang Yin in brilliance or Wen Zhengming in constancy, but made 'wildness' a contested-by-no-one summit in their shared city; and his deepest principle was to reverse the order of judgment: spirit before shape, nature before strategy, posthumous fame before present opinion — all his life he kept only the brush, entrusting everything else to his nature
civilization_zh: 明代中期——吴中的天才被科场与礼法双重围困，把狂放经营成一门艺术、把异相署成名字，在酒与笔墨之间为'性情'赢得全部尊严
civilization_en: The middle Ming — the talent of Wu besieged at once by the examinations and by propriety, who made wildness into an art and signed his own deformity, winning between wine and ink the full dignity of 'nature'
roles_en: First of the Four Talents of Wu

cross_references.description_zh: 祝允明与唐寅是同代同城的镜像：同为吴中才子、同为科场所弃（唐寅科场案、祝允明五次落第）、同以'狂'为标记——唐寅以才与画在市场上重建，祝允明以狂草与性情在笔墨里自持；唐寅的狂是绝境中的自嘲（桃花庵），祝允明的狂是天性的舒展（枝指生）——对照命题：同一个'狂'字，一个写的是被夺走的人生，一个写的是不肯被夺走的性情。
cross_references.description_en: Zhu Yunming and Tang Yin are mirrors in the same city and age: both talents of Wu, both cast off by the examinations — Tang by the scandal, Zhu by five failures — both marked by 'wildness'; Tang rebuilt in the market with genius and painting, Zhu held himself within brush and ink with cursive and nature; Tang's wildness is self-mockery at a dead end (the Peach Blossom Cottage), Zhu's is the unfolding of an inborn nature (the Branched Finger); the contrast: the same word 'wild' — one writes a life taken from him, the other a nature that refused to be taken.

cross_references.description_zh: 祝允明与文徵明是吴门的双璧与两端：同为吴中四才子，一个以'狂'立身（兴会、狼藉、颓放），一个以'恒'立身（日课、谨严、传灯）——文徵明的草书出自祝允明指授，祝允明晚年落魄时文徵明始终执弟子礼；两人合起来示范了天才的两种治理：让性情全权发展（祝），把性情编入制度（文）——并峙而非对立。
cross_references.description_en: Zhu Yunming and Wen Zhengming are the twin jewels and the two ends of the Wu school: both of the Four Talents, one standing on 'wildness' (the rousing, the strewn stroke, the abandon), the other on 'constancy' (the daily course, the discipline, the transmission); Wen's cursive was taught by Zhu, and in Zhu's late poverty Wen kept always a pupil's respect; together they demonstrate the two governances of talent — letting nature rule entire (Zhu), and binding nature into institution (Wen) — standing alongside, never opposed.

cross_references.description_zh: 祝允明与杜牧同负旷世之才而仕途皆不得志，方向相反：杜牧把失意烧成诗的锋利（十年一觉扬州梦），在公牍之外以绝句自证；祝允明把失意活成书体的自由（点画狼藉），在科场之外以笔墨自持——杜牧的失败需要一个'梦醒'的解释框架，祝允明的失败被整件退出、不再解释——对照命题：对同一个失败，可以留下解释（杜牧），也可以直接退场（祝允明）。
cross_references.description_en: Zhu Yunming and Du Mu carry talents of the age and meet like disappointment in office, facing opposite ways: Du Mu burns defeat into the sharpness of verse ('ten years a dream in Yangzhou'), proving himself in quatrains beyond the paperwork; Zhu lives defeat into the freedom of a script (strewn strokes), holding himself in brush and ink beyond the examinations — Du Mu's failure needs a frame of 'waking from the dream'; Zhu's failure is exited whole, needing no explanation — the contrast: at the same failure, one leaves an explanation, the other leaves the field.
